what: The first attempt to run the 512-rank PI-atm case on Derecho's GPU nodes (8 nodes x 64 ranks) failed at initialisation for the CPU image with nothing armed as much as for the CUDA image; the same layout on CPU nodes fails the same way.  Kept as evidence that the model, as built, depends on 128 ranks a node.
layout: select=8:ncpus=64:mpiprocs=64 (GPU nodes: ngpus=4:gpu_type=a100); every validated run of this case uses select=4:ncpus=64:mpiprocs=128

native_image.p34: build/pi_cam_promoted_p34 (FTorch on a CUDA libtorch, commit ddff0d18)

outcome: GPU nodes, both images: a handful of ranks (4, 5, 13 on the first node; 453, 485 on the last) died of SIGSEGV in Fortran during CAM initialisation, right after the initial-condition field listing, before cam_history's BLDFLD; one run showed glibc 'corrupted size vs. prev_size'; the other ranks raised the collective BoundaryReplayError and exited 255.
CPU nodes, 8 x 64, p33: rank 0 died of the same SIGSEGV at the same point and the job hung until qdel (7538643).

CPU nodes, 8 x 64, p33, FOR_IGNORE_EXCEPTIONS=TRUE (7539071): no fault, but the initial CAM export differed from the recorded replay boundary on 122 of 512 ranks (cam_out.a2x_rattr hashes; ranks 89-108 among them), so the run refused to start.

Rank 0 under gdb (7569084): no fault (the layout under the debugger changes), but the initial CAM export differed from the recording on 8 ranks: attribute 3 of cam_out.a2x_rattr is inf in the 128-a-node recording and 0.0 here -- a value computed from memory CAM leaves uninitialised, which the two layouts happen to fill differently.
MALLOC_PERTURB_=255, every malloc block zero-filled (7569202): the same export difference; the uninitialised value is not on the malloc heap.

With the export check off (7572486 CPU, 7575839 and 7575840 GPU): the model dies at initialization or at step 0 on a few ranks (SIGSEGV at rank 499 while reading the DMS tracer data; an abort with a core on rank 456 after the initial-condition listing); 7575840 then hung until its walltime.  The node's core_pattern pipes cores to systemd-coredump, out of reach.
probe: a GPU node (7538626): stack unlimited, 512 GB, driver 580.65, four A100s, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES set by PBS; the p34 image dlopens there.
diagnosis: Not the GPU nodes: the same failures appear on CPU nodes once the layout is 64 ranks a node.  What changes with the layout is memory placement, not the decomposition, so a layout-dependent memory fault in the image or the control layer is the likely cause (uninitialised or fixed-address memory whose content the 128-a-node layout happened to make consistent).  Not resolved here.  The export difference comes from memory CAM reads before it writes, off the malloc heap (static or stack storage); the faults are its other symptoms.  16 ranks a GPU with MPS, which needs this layout, is measured only outside the model (1.57 ms a call on one node).
disposition: The GPU measurement is retried on the validated layout: 4 GPU nodes with 128 ranks over the 64 cores' two hardware threads each, the same for the CPU-path comparison.  The 64-a-node fault is a separate finding to chase.
